fixes.explanation: Paul says people are "…justified freely by His grace through the redemption that is in Christ Jesus." Freely means as a gift, so there's no payback plan hiding in the fine print. No invoice, no installments, nothing taped to the back. False is the right call, baker.

Baker, that's the pair! Paul says God did this "…so as to be just and to justify the one who has faith in Jesus." You'd think staying just and justifying someone would pull in opposite directions, like two cooks fighting over one oven. But Paul puts both in one sentence and doesn't make God pick one.

Faith goes in the second blank, baker! Paul says, "No, but on that of faith." Boasting gets shut out, and faith is the principle he names. I tried boasting about my own cookies once, and the dough just stared at me.

Birth is a fun guess, but Paul doesn't name it. He asks, "On what principle? On that of works? No, but on that of faith." Birth never makes it into that verse, so it goes back on the cooling rack. Works and faith fill the blanks.
Money, huh? Paul never reaches for his wallet in this verse. He asks, "On what principle? On that of works? No, but on that of faith." Works and faith fill the blanks, no cash required.

Strength sounds like it could fit, and I'd love to flex my mustache and call it the answer. But Paul doesn't use it. He asks, "On what principle? On that of works? No, but on that of faith." Works goes in the first blank and faith in the second.
